svg.text: Allegro | Consecutive MMA issue and block prefetch
Single CTA · Three ordered command records · Two input contexts · Four cores with 64 complete dot lanes each
Command admission and B source reads
Acquire pin and select B partition by ID
16 B atom across four adjacent banks
Sample at g, deliver from g+2
Full atoms for FP16/BF16, masks otherwise
K passes through, N transposes to column order
Cores accept separately, last frees slot
An eight-column FP16/BF16 block takes sixteen 16 B reads. Adjacent commands may own the two slots. Each core checks its partition and overwrite permission.
Per-core inputs / Reuse each operand after its own last read
Overwrite each block after its final op_load
Same-address C[j] waits for old D[j] ACK success
2 × 128 B of scale A per core
Two snapshots in 4 KiB shared scale B
Select r, j, and their scales
First load in lockstep, then independent
The first microtile can use installed B0. Publish a WS collector only after full installation on all four cores. Read shared B source data once.
8 rows × 8 columns per core per cycle
Different families can issue back to back
1 KiB per slot, selected by result tag
Release data slot on last write acceptance
Accept at w, write at w+1
Settle the original ID and block j
Release dependency after all required writes succeed
Wide and K32 share the input stages by default. Results retire in issue order. Trailing writes and the pin retain the original instruction ID.
All reads, computation, writes, and ACKs
for this core and ID have settled
Join four cores, loader, and snapshots
Return pin and report ID to tracker
Accept one final completion per ID
The data path hands off first issue. The tracker receives final completion. After stop, drain all three records, partial deliveries, presented requests, and write ACKs.
Steady-state N128 FP16 in-place accumulation / Aligned K-major, warm, uncontended. Numbers denote handshake edges.
Next C0 Grant 58/59 → return 61/62 → load R_OP at 63 → first dot at 64
Next C1 Grant 62/63 → return 65/66 → load R_OP at 67 → first dot of block 1 at 68
Previous writes Last result enters D at 68 → writes accepted at 69/70 → final write commits at 71 → final ACK at 72
Previous completion Accept local_done at 73 → return pin at 74 → earliest tracker acceptance at 75
Both commands share 128 B/cycle of SMEM. For other layouts, competing clients, late ACKs, or output stalls, use actual handshake edges.
TMA / One walker, with all copies sharing a peak of 128 B/cycle
Hold ID and data on a stalled return
Load takes a slot on return
Store reserves a slot before reading SMEM
Match actual write ACKs by original tag
Loads move right and stores move left. Release the data slot on acceptance of the final SMEM group write or the GMEM line write.
Orange arrows show completion. Loads collect per-group SMEM write ACKs and stores collect GMEM write ACKs. Store .read may complete once all source reads finish.
